utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please read this letter and tell us whether you are familiar with the letter?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the subject matter involved, and I'm sure that this is authentic in terms of what we had asked the warden to do, that is to say, to ask the Ministry of Justice for this, because we had major problems with oil, and we had to keep the farms going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, can you see at the end of this document a seal and a signature? Is that the seal of the KP Dom, and is that the signature of the warden?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I can read here Kazneno-Popravni, and then there's something illegible. But the signature is the warden's for sure, but the stamp is barely legible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, would you look underneath the letterhead where it says Kazneno-Popravni Dom Foca, there is a number and the number has not been entered. Can you explain this to me, why the number was not written?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: This could be a third copy of this particular letter, because a letter of this kind is written in three copies. One goes to the addressee; the other copy remains in the files, and that's where it gets a number for the files; and this third copy remains for the person who had actually written it so that he could keep it for his own files. That's the way I see it, because I don't see any other reason why it wouldn't have a number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether letters and decisions were recorded in the same register in the same way at that time in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: It depended on the contents of the letter concerned. If that is correspondence between the KP Dom and the Ministry, it is only natural that it is registered in the book. If this is correspondence related, for example, to some other matters like plain letters, then it wasn't compulsory. And if these were decisions that involved financial obligations, then it had to be registered in the so-called protocol of financial obligations, and that is also where travel orders went, travel authorisations, bills, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't be needing this document any more. Could the usher please show the witness -- I'm talking about number 90 and 90-1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please take a look at this and tell us what is this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: Travel authorisation for an official trip, the warden of the KP Dom to travel to Bijeljina to attend a meeting. Mode of travel used, vehicle, GZ47755; and also the amount of money involved, 5.000 dinars. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: There has to be another sheet of paper in here where it says "For the Cashier," that is to say, when he takes this particular amount allocated to him, that is to say that this part of it is inserted here, is used by the employee going on an official trip to collect his advance and leave that at the cashier's, whereas this remaining piece of paper is taken by him and then when he returns, in this part all the travel expenses involved during that journey are calculated. I think that this is a perfectly correct travel authorisation. It is registered as number 178/ -- probably 92, and it is number 10, number 313 as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just clarify something. The inside of this piece of paper that you just folded now, is that actually this second sheet that you are holding in your hand right now?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I haven't got that piece of paper that goes to the cashier. I just have the first page, and then the second page in terms of the advance I don't have, and then I have the third page where the calculation is made of the travel expenses incurred. I can't see it here in this travel authorisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? The travel authorisation consisted of a folded sheet of paper consisting of two pages, so to speak, which actually had four pages if you look at both sides, and then there was an additional sheet of paper that was put between those two pages and that was handed over to the cashier when this person mentioned was given the advance that he was supposed to be paid prior to his journey?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for things to be perfectly clear, could the usher please give me that particular copy back, and I'm going to give the witness a copy of ID D90, where on one single page, all the pages involved were photocopied, so that everybody in the courtroom understood what we were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You may be assuming too much, Mr. Vasic, when you say that. Why are we going into such excruciating detail about these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wouldn't want to go into all the details. However, my learned friends actually put questions related to these travel authorisations, as to whether this was a folded piece of paper and what was inside. Especially in view of the next exhibit that I will be showing to the witness, and our learned friends had questions in relation to that and certain objections as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if there is something you're about to reach, we won't stop you, but it has been excruciating, I've got to say. You proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, and I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, what you have there in front of you, is that an original travel authorisation the way you had put it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: You returned to me the same document you gave me a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're right. It's the same document. However, if we were to fold it in half right now, would that be the form for a travel authorisation that was used in those days?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: What is missing is the piece of paper that is inside, that is submitted to the cashier in order to obtain money, and what you gave me here, in addition, is just an invoice or, rather, a hotel bill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you look at the signature on page 1 of this travel authorisation? Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: You mean this, what I have right now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, ID D90.

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: On page 1, this is my signature. On page 3, again my signature, Mico Krnojelac, and Mico Krnojelac, rather, Micun Jokanovic and Mico Krnojelac, who received the money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Since you signed this travel authorisation, do you know whether Mr. Milorad Krnojelac travelled to Bijeljina to attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Milorad Krnojelac travelled to Bijeljina, because upon his return, I was returned to the Dom because I had some business to finish precisely upon the orders that he had received at that meeting in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the inside of this document, this travel authorisation. Can you tell us how much time Mr. Milorad Krnojelac spent on this trip?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: He departed on the 15th of September at 10.00. He returned on the 17th of September at 1830 hours. He spent 48 hours travelling, that is to say, two per diems plus 8.30, and according to our rules, he was entitled to two and a half per diems, and a per diem was then 1.500 dinars, and that is 3.750 dinars. Then there is a hotel bill there amounting to 2.950. So that is a total of 6.700. And the advance he received prior to his journey is subtracted from that, and then 1.700 is the remaining amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't be needing this particular document any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you mention that had after Mr. Milorad Krnojelac came from Bjelinja, you were assigned certain tasks. What were they?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, I was given the task to find the report that we made when we came to the Dom, that is to say, in terms of damage estimates, that I should establish for the period between April and September and October how much we actually traded, what amount of goods we gave, and what we received in return, and also I was asked about some other economic indicators concerning the activity of the Drina Economic Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did Mr. Milorad Krnojelac need that survey of activity of the Drina unit that you made?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: He told me that all corps, Prosecutors' offices, all institutions got orders from the minister that they should submit reports on their activity and work in various KP Doms and their attached economic units, because all the correction facilities, all the KP Doms, had their attached economic units as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show ID D86 to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please take a look and tell me whether you find this document familiar?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I do. I drafted it. This is a copy. This is a table of sales and procured goods in the Drina Economic Unit for the period from the 29th of May until the 15th of October, 1992. I did this so that the warden of the Dom could submit a report to the Ministry of Justice about his work in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the last page. When was this document compiled, and why was it not signed?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: This is a copy of my report, the one I submitted to the warden. However, in addition to the warden, all heads of working units and services asked for a copy, and it was therefore retyped, and you happened to get this kind of copy that was not signed at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, on the basis of what did you compile this review?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I did that on the basis of bookkeeping, on the basis of records kept, invoices, according to the buyers mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at item 4.

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date by that item, that is, the 16th of June, and also item 21, please, the 3rd of October. Can you tell us -- just a minute, I'm sorry. I didn't mean item 21. I meant item 11, the 31st of August. In this period, do you not have trade with Serbia and Montenegro displayed here?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this interim between the end of June and --

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I have here the 16th of June, sending goods to Belgrade department stores, and then there's the 16th of July, so there is a period that's vacant. And then the 8th of August --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the 16th of June and the 16th of July, did you take goods to Yugoslavia or bring goods from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: On the basis of what I can see from this survey, in that month there weren't any purchases in or from or for Yugoslavia because I haven't got any invoices to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why in this period there weren't any sales and why goods didn't go to and from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I do know. I do know why. In this period, our director was absent, and none of us would decide at his own initiative to buy or sell something because we were not authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that your director was not there. Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: When we're talking about this period, both the warden and the director for me is Milorad Krnojelac. That is one and the same person because we did not have a separate warden and a separate director.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Milorad Krnojelac then, in the second half of June and the first half of July, 1992; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO DRAKUL
utterances.text: I think that in that period his child had had an accident, that he was in hospital in Belgrade. For sure I don't know the exact date, but I think it must have been the end of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid it's 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not afraid at all, Mr. Vasic. Do you think we're going to go on for very much more with this examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think not more than 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. We'll resume again at 9.30 in the morning. We are still in this courtroom tomorrow.
